title: Fieldwise Anomaly Sampling & Reconciliation Notes
content:
Purpose
Quick personal playbook for sampling and reconciling field-level anomalies in tabular ingestion. Focus is on mixed-type cells, embedded JSON strings, weird currency formats, and id-like freeform text. Aim: fast audit sample -> heuristics -> small rule set -> adjudication protocol.

Principles (short)
- Prioritize fields with high downstream model sensitivity (prompt inputs, ids, prompts).
- Prefer stratified sampling by value frequency + length buckets (short, medium, long).
- Capture both syntactic oddities (unicode, control chars) and semantic anomalies (impossible currencies, future dates).
- Keep rules conservative; when in doubt mark for human labeler/adjudicator.

Sampling recipe
1) Top-100k by cardinality: sample 500 random rows across value-length quantiles.
2) Tail bucket (values occurring <=3x): sample all if <=2k, otherwise random 1,000.
3) Outlier numeric detection: z-score over numeric-parseable subset, sample top 200 by abs(z) and 200 by highest parsing failure rate.
4) Embedded-JSON detection: regex for ^\{.*\}$ or starting with '[' and JSON.parse fails; sample 300.

Example SQL snippets (Postgres-ish)
- detect possible embedded JSON:
  SELECT id, field FROM table WHERE field ~ '^\s*\{|^\s*\[' LIMIT 500;
- frequency tail:
  WITH freq AS (SELECT field, count(*) AS c FROM table GROUP BY field) SELECT field FROM freq WHERE c <= 3 ORDER BY random() LIMIT 1000;
- length quantiles:
  SELECT percentile_disc(ARRAY[0.25,0.5,0.75]) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY length(field)) FROM table;

Heuristics quick hits
- Currency: strip whitespace + common symbols, then if not matching ^[0-9,.]+$ -> flag. Watch for thousands-sep ambiguity (1,234 vs 1.234).
- IDs that look like UUIDs but have missing dashes: accept if hex length matches 32.
- Dates: prefer ISO parse; catch two-digit years; treat anything with '/' ambiguous.
- Embedded HTML: detect '<[a-z][\s\S]*>' frequency, treat as noise unless field is explicitly markup.
- Control chars/zero-width: if length after trimming < original length by >30% -> inspect.

Labeling guidance for ambiguous cases (for adjudicators)
- Mixed numeric/text (e.g., "12,000 USD" vs "12k"): normalize to canonical numeric with currency metadata when possible; otherwise label as ABSTAIN for numeric fields.
- Postal codes vs short ids: if alpha-numeric length <= 6 and contains spaces -> lean toward postal code only if there's geo context.
- Embedded JSON that is malformed but clearly key-value: try to salvage keys into structured columns; otherwise mark broken-json and add sample to dev ticket.

Imputation rules (order of ops)
1) If canonical default exists (e.g., country default for regionless rows) use it but set imputation_source=DEFAULT.
2) If single-candidate from other columns (e.g., country inferred from phone cc) set imputation_source=INFERRED and note confidence.
3) If no reliable inference, leave NULL and label for human follow-up.

Adjudication protocol (2-pass microflow)
- Pass A (rapid): single labeler marks likely-fixable and adds short rationale. Use flag FAST_FIX.
- Pass B (adjudicator): review FAST_FIX items; if >80% agree on same rule across sampled 100 -> convert to automated rule and create PR in data-tools.
- Track edgecases in a shared spreadsheet; include example row, attempted fix, and unit test example.

Quick regex cheats (for local tests)
- detect currency-ish: /(^|\s)[\$£€¥]|(USD|EUR|GBP)/i
- strip invisible: /[\u200B-\u200F\uFEFF]/g
- almost-uuid (no dashes): /^[0-9a-fA-F]{32}$/

Open questions / TODOs
- How to surface imputed-source metadata downstream of model training? (add column imputed_by + confidence as metadata)
- Should we aggressively normalize thousands separators for all numeric-like fields? Risk: EU vs US formats.
- Build small CLI that runs sample queries and emits a single HTML summary for triage (JIRA-IL-487 tracking).

Notes to self (one-liners)
- When adding a rule, write a unit test with 3 positives and 3 negatives.
- Pair with Samir for 30m to go through 50 tail rows from spreadsheets dataset.
- Push small regex fix as quick PR to data-tools, then run rollout on a staging snapshot first.

Link references (copy here to avoid hunting later)
- Confluence: /display/DATA/Cleanup+Patterns (internal)
- Jira: IL-487 ("Field anomaly sampling infra")
- PR reference: github.com/redwood-inference/data-tools/pull/312

End.
